spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m1p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, NumStations, NumUnits

None == 0
Stations == 1 .. NumStations
Units == 1 .. NumUnits

\* Each unit's paperwork is filed at one fixed home station on the ring.
HomeOf(u) == 1 + ((u - 1) % NumStations)
NextStation(s) == IF s = NumStations THEN 1 ELSE s + 1

VARIABLES token, ledger, draft, snapshot, outstanding

vars == <<token, ledger, draft, snapshot, outstanding>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in [Instances -> Stations]
  /\ ledger \subseteq Units
  /\ draft \in [Instances -> Units \cup {None}]
  /\ snapshot \in [Instances -> SUBSET Units]
  /\ outstanding \subseteq Units

\* Nothing that has left the outstanding queue may be missing from the shared
\* ledger, and a live draft never carries a snapshot the ledger has lost.
NoLostUpdate ==
  /\ \A u \in Units : u \notin outstanding => u \in ledger
  /\ \A i \in Instances : draft[i] # None => snapshot[i] \subseteq ledger

Init ==
  /\ token \in [Instances -> Stations]
  /\ ledger = {}
  /\ draft = [i \in Instances |-> None]
  /\ snapshot = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
  /\ outstanding = Units

Rotate(i) ==
  /\ draft[i] = None
  /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![i] = NextStation(token[i])]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, draft, snapshot, outstanding>>

Claim(i, u) ==
  /\ draft[i] = None
  /\ u \in outstanding
  /\ token[i] = HomeOf(u)
  /\ \A j \in Instances : draft[j] # u
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![i] = u]
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![i] = ledger]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, ledger, outstanding>>

\* A post is refused unless the drafter still sees the current ledger.
Post(i) ==
  /\ draft[i] # None
  /\ snapshot[i] = ledger
  /\ ledger' = snapshot[i] \cup {draft[i]}
  /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {draft[i]}
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![i] = None]
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

Discard(i) ==
  /\ draft[i] # None
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![i] = None]
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, ledger, outstanding>>

Next ==
  \E i \in Instances :
    \/ Rotate(i)
    \/ Post(i)
    \/ Discard(i)
    \/ \E u \in Units : Claim(i, u)

SomeRotate == \E i \in Instances : Rotate(i)
SomeClaim == \E i \in Instances, u \in Units : Claim(i, u)
SomePost == \E i \in Instances : Post(i)
SomeDiscard == \E i \in Instances : Discard(i)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SomeRotate)
  /\ WF_vars(SomeDiscard)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeClaim)
  /\ SF_vars(SomePost)

EveryUnitEventuallyPosted ==
  \A u \in Units : (u \in outstanding) ~> (u \in ledger)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {trkA, trkB}
    NumStations = 2
    NumUnits = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
PROPERTY EveryUnitEventuallyPosted
nl:
A regional blood-bank inventory tracker is operated by two independent tracker
instances that share a single pool of blood units. Every unit adjustment must
land in one shared ledger record, and no adjustment may be silently overwritten
by a concurrent writer.

Each instance drives its own token that walks a fixed ring of intake stations.
A unit's paperwork is filed at one fixed home station on that ring, so an
instance can only pick a unit up while its token is parked at that unit's home
station.

Four things can happen. Rotate: an idle instance advances its token one step
around the ring. Claim: an instance whose token sits at a unit's home station
takes that outstanding unit as its working draft and copies the ledger it can
currently see into a snapshot; a unit already held as some instance's draft
cannot be claimed again. Post: an instance holding a draft rewrites the ledger
as its snapshot plus the drafted unit, but only if that snapshot still equals
the live ledger, and the unit then leaves the outstanding queue. Discard: an
instance abandons its draft, leaving the unit outstanding and the ledger
untouched.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every unit that has left the outstanding queue is present in
the shared ledger, and any instance still holding a draft carries a snapshot
that is contained in the live ledger.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every outstanding unit is eventually posted into the shared
ledger.

---- MODULE W4Od16m9p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bins, Scripts, NoBin, NoRx, MaxEpoch

ASSUME NoBin \notin Bins
ASSUME NoRx \notin Scripts

VARIABLES epoch, active, holder, slotOf, quoteBin, quoteEpoch

vars == <<epoch, active, holder, slotOf, quoteBin, quoteEpoch>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ active \subseteq Bins
  /\ holder \in [Bins -> Scripts \cup {NoRx}]
  /\ slotOf \in [Scripts -> Bins \cup {NoBin}]
  /\ quoteBin \in [Scripts -> Bins \cup {NoBin}]
  /\ quoteEpoch \in [Scripts -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

\* The bin-side and script-side views of the wall must agree, and a bin the
\* live configuration has retired may not still be holding a prescription.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  /\ \A r \in Scripts : slotOf[r] # NoBin => holder[slotOf[r]] = r
  /\ \A b \in Bins : holder[b] # NoRx => slotOf[holder[b]] = b
  /\ \A b \in Bins : holder[b] # NoRx => b \in active

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ active = Bins
  /\ holder = [b \in Bins |-> NoRx]
  /\ slotOf = [r \in Scripts |-> NoBin]
  /\ quoteBin = [r \in Scripts |-> NoBin]
  /\ quoteEpoch = [r \in Scripts |-> 0]

\* A republish resizes the wall and evicts whatever sat in a retired bin.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E na \in (SUBSET Bins) \ {{}} :
       /\ na # active
       /\ active' = na
       /\ holder' = [b \in Bins |-> IF b \in na THEN holder[b] ELSE NoRx]
       /\ slotOf' = [r \in Scripts |->
            IF slotOf[r] \notin na THEN NoBin ELSE slotOf[r]]
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quoteBin, quoteEpoch>>

Quote(r, b) ==
  /\ slotOf[r] = NoBin
  /\ quoteBin[r] = NoBin
  /\ b \in active
  /\ holder[b] = NoRx
  /\ quoteBin' = [quoteBin EXCEPT ![r] = b]
  /\ quoteEpoch' = [quoteEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, holder, slotOf>>

\* A quote is honoured only in the epoch that issued it.
Commit(r) ==
  /\ quoteBin[r] # NoBin
  /\ quoteEpoch[r] = epoch
  /\ quoteBin[r] \in active
  /\ holder[quoteBin[r]] = NoRx
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![quoteBin[r]] = r]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![r] = quoteBin[r]]
  /\ quoteBin' = [quoteBin EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, quoteEpoch>>

DropQuote(r) ==
  /\ quoteBin[r] # NoBin
  /\ quoteEpoch[r] # epoch
  /\ quoteBin' = [quoteBin EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, holder, slotOf, quoteEpoch>>

Collect(r) ==
  /\ slotOf[r] # NoBin
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![slotOf[r]] = NoRx]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, active, quoteBin, quoteEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E r \in Scripts :
       \/ Commit(r)
       \/ DropQuote(r)
       \/ Collect(r)
       \/ \E b \in Bins : Quote(r, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bins = {binA, binB}
    Scripts = {rx1, rx2}
    NoBin = noBin
    NoRx = noRx
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser fills a wall of numbered pickup bins. Its
controller republishes the wall's configuration under a strictly increasing
epoch number, and a republish may take bins out of service or bring bins back
in, so the usable capacity changes while prescriptions are being routed.

The dispenser keeps two views that must agree: for each bin, which prescription
is sitting in it, and for each prescription, which bin it was routed to.

Five things can happen. Reconfigure: the controller bumps the epoch, installs a
new non-empty set of in-service bins, and pulls every prescription out of a bin
that the new configuration retires. Quote: an unrouted prescription with no
outstanding quote is offered an in-service bin that is currently empty, and the
quote is stamped with the epoch in force. Commit: a quoted prescription is
actually dropped into its quoted bin, but only if the stamped epoch is still
the current epoch, the bin is still in service, and the bin is still empty; the
quote is then cleared. DropQuote: a quote stamped with a superseded epoch is
torn up. Collect: a patient takes a prescription out of its bin, emptying the
bin and unrouting the prescription.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bin-to-prescription and prescription-to-bin views always
agree with each other, and no bin that is out of service ever holds a
prescription -- so no bin is ever handed to two prescriptions at once.

---- MODULE W4Od3m8p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, Payments, Admin, NoOne

ASSUME Admin \notin Banks
ASSUME NoOne \notin Banks

Agents == Banks \cup {Admin}

VARIABLES coarse, fine, settled, worklist, override

vars == <<coarse, fine, settled, worklist, override>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Agents \cup {NoOne}
  /\ fine \in [Payments -> Agents \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ settled \subseteq Payments
  /\ worklist \subseteq Payments
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

\* A wire is irreversible: the payment must have left the worklist and no
\* participant may still be holding a fine claim that could wire it again.
SettledStaysSettled ==
  /\ settled \cap worklist = {}
  /\ \A p \in Payments : p \in settled => fine[p] = NoOne

Init ==
  /\ coarse = NoOne
  /\ fine = [p \in Payments |-> NoOne]
  /\ settled = {}
  /\ worklist = Payments
  /\ override = FALSE

\* Coarse claim on the batch first, fine claim on a single line second.
TakeBatch(b) ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ coarse = NoOne
  /\ coarse' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, settled, worklist, override>>

TakeLine(b, p) ==
  /\ coarse = b
  /\ p \in worklist
  /\ fine[p] = NoOne
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![p] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, settled, worklist, override>>

Wire(b, p) ==
  /\ fine[p] = b
  /\ p \in worklist
  /\ settled' = settled \cup {p}
  /\ worklist' = worklist \ {p}
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![p] = NoOne]
  /\ coarse' = NoOne
  /\ UNCHANGED override

StandDown(b) ==
  /\ coarse = b
  /\ coarse' = NoOne
  /\ fine' = [p \in Payments |-> IF fine[p] = b THEN NoOne ELSE fine[p]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, worklist, override>>

\* The duty officer outranks both claim levels.
AdminSeize ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ override' = TRUE
  /\ coarse' = Admin
  /\ fine' = [p \in Payments |-> IF fine[p] \in Banks THEN NoOne ELSE fine[p]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, worklist>>

AdminWire(p) ==
  /\ override
  /\ p \in worklist
  /\ fine[p] = NoOne
  /\ settled' = settled \cup {p}
  /\ worklist' = worklist \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, override>>

AdminRelease ==
  /\ override
  /\ override' = FALSE
  /\ coarse' = NoOne
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, settled, worklist>>

Next ==
  \/ AdminSeize
  \/ AdminRelease
  \/ \E p \in Payments : AdminWire(p)
  \/ \E b \in Banks :
       \/ TakeBatch(b)
       \/ StandDown(b)
       \/ \E p \in Payments : TakeLine(b, p) \/ Wire(b, p)

SomeTakeBatch == \E b \in Banks : TakeBatch(b)
SomeTakeLine == \E b \in Banks, p \in Payments : TakeLine(b, p)
SomeWire == \E b \in Banks, p \in Payments : Wire(b, p)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AdminRelease)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeTakeBatch)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeTakeLine)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeWire)

EveryPaymentEventuallyWired ==
  \A p \in Payments : (p \in worklist) ~> (p \in settled)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bkA, bkB}
    Payments = {pm1, pm2}
    Admin = duty
    NoOne = none
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SettledStaysSettled
PROPERTY EveryPaymentEventuallyWired
nl:
A clearing house runs an interbank settlement batch. Each payment in the batch
must be wired out, and a wire is irreversible: once the funds leave, there is
no way to take them back, so a payment must never be wired a second time.

Access to the batch is hierarchical. A member bank first takes the coarse claim
on the whole batch, and only then may it take the fine claim on one individual
payment line. A duty officer at the clearing house holds a privileged override
that outranks both levels.

Seven things can happen. TakeBatch: a bank with no override in force takes the
free coarse claim. TakeLine: the bank holding the coarse claim takes the free
fine claim on a payment that is still on the worklist. Wire: a bank holding the
fine claim on a worklist payment sends the funds, which moves the payment off
the worklist into the settled record, drops its fine claim, and releases the
coarse claim. StandDown: the bank holding the coarse claim gives it up and
drops every fine claim it was holding, wiring nothing. AdminSeize: the duty
officer engages the override, takes the coarse claim, and strips every bank's
fine claim. AdminWire: with the override engaged, the duty officer wires a
worklist payment whose fine claim is free. AdminRelease: the duty officer
disengages the override and leaves the coarse claim free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A payment is never both settled and still on the worklist, and
no participant holds the fine claim on a payment that has already been wired,
so no payment can be wired twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every payment still on the worklist is eventually wired.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Payments, Slots, NoPay, NoSlot, MaxTerm

ASSUME NoPay \notin Payments
ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots

VARIABLES term, myTerm, down, occupant, slotOf

vars == <<term, myTerm, down, occupant, slotOf>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ myTerm \in [Nodes -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
  /\ down \subseteq Nodes
  /\ occupant \in [Slots -> Payments \cup {NoPay}]
  /\ slotOf \in [Payments -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

\* A node writes the books only while its own term is still the live term.
IsLeader(n) == term > 0 /\ myTerm[n] = term

\* The slot book and the payment book must be exact inverses, so no settlement
\* slot can ever be carrying two payments at once.
SlotBooksAgree ==
  /\ \A s \in Slots : occupant[s] # NoPay => slotOf[occupant[s]] = s
  /\ \A p \in Payments : slotOf[p] # NoSlot => occupant[slotOf[p]] = p

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ myTerm = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
  /\ down = {}
  /\ occupant = [s \in Slots |-> NoPay]
  /\ slotOf = [p \in Payments |-> NoSlot]

\* Any live node may raise the term; the displaced leader is never told.
Elect(n) ==
  /\ n \notin down
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ ~IsLeader(n)
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ myTerm' = [myTerm EXCEPT ![n] = term + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<down, occupant, slotOf>>

Fail(n) ==
  /\ n \notin down
  /\ down' = down \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, myTerm, occupant, slotOf>>

Restart(n) ==
  /\ n \in down
  /\ down' = down \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, myTerm, occupant, slotOf>>

Allocate(n, p, s) ==
  /\ IsLeader(n)
  /\ n \notin down
  /\ slotOf[p] = NoSlot
  /\ occupant[s] = NoPay
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![p] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, myTerm, down>>

Recall(n, p) ==
  /\ IsLeader(n)
  /\ n \notin down
  /\ slotOf[p] # NoSlot
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![slotOf[p]] = NoPay]
  /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![p] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, myTerm, down>>

Next ==
  \E n \in Nodes :
    \/ Elect(n)
    \/ Fail(n)
    \/ Restart(n)
    \/ \E p \in Payments :
         \/ Recall(n, p)
         \/ \E s \in Slots : Allocate(n, p, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
nl:
A clearing house settles an interbank batch by placing each payment into one of
a fixed number of settlement slots in the day's timetable. A slot carries at
most one payment, and the timetable is kept in two books that must mirror each
other: the slot book says which payment sits in each slot, and the payment book
says which slot each payment was given.

Only the elected settlement leader may write the books. Leadership is carried by
a term number: any live node may raise the term and take the leadership for
itself, and a node is the leader only while its own recorded term equals the
live term. A node can fail silently -- no announcement is made and the other
nodes are not told -- so the surviving nodes simply elect a successor under a
higher term, and the failed node's stale term locks it out if it ever comes
back.

Five things can happen. Elect: a live node that is not already the leader raises
the term by one and records that new term as its own. Fail: a node stops
silently. Restart: a stopped node comes back up, still carrying whatever term it
had. Allocate: the live leader places a payment that has no slot into a slot
that has no payment, writing both books. Recall: the live leader takes a payment
back out of its slot, clearing both books.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot book and the payment book are always exact inverses of
each other, so no settlement slot is ever allocated to two payments at once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Workers, Students, NoOne, MaxGen, MaxSeats

ASSUME NoOne \notin Workers

VARIABLES holder, gen, writer, stamp, seated, cap

vars == <<holder, gen, writer, stamp, seated, cap>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in Workers \cup {NoOne}
  /\ gen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ writer \in [Students -> Workers \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ stamp \in [Students -> 0 .. MaxGen]
  /\ seated \subseteq Students
  /\ cap \in 1 .. MaxSeats

Decided == {s \in Students : writer[s] # NoOne}

\* A decision stamped with the live generation must name the worker that still
\* holds the lease; older stamps are retired and can never be attributed.
NoStaleWriter ==
  /\ \A s \in Students : writer[s] # NoOne => stamp[s] <= gen
  /\ \A s \in Students : (writer[s] # NoOne /\ stamp[s] = gen) => writer[s] = holder
  /\ seated \subseteq Decided

Init ==
  /\ holder = NoOne
  /\ gen = 0
  /\ writer = [s \in Students |-> NoOne]
  /\ stamp = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ seated = {}
  /\ cap \in 1 .. MaxSeats

Grant(w) ==
  /\ holder = NoOne
  /\ holder' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, writer, stamp, seated, cap>>

\* Expiry retires the generation, so nothing already written stays attributable.
Expire ==
  /\ holder # NoOne
  /\ gen < MaxGen
  /\ holder' = NoOne
  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<writer, stamp, seated, cap>>

Admit(w, s) ==
  /\ holder = w
  /\ writer[s] = NoOne
  /\ Cardinality(seated) < cap
  /\ seated' = seated \cup {s}
  /\ writer' = [writer EXCEPT ![s] = w]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![s] = gen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, cap>>

Refuse(w, s) ==
  /\ holder = w
  /\ writer[s] = NoOne
  /\ Cardinality(seated) >= cap
  /\ writer' = [writer EXCEPT ![s] = w]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![s] = gen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, seated, cap>>

\* The registrar edits capacity while registration is running.
Resize ==
  /\ \E c \in 1 .. MaxSeats : c # cap /\ cap' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, writer, stamp, seated>>

Next ==
  \/ Expire
  \/ Resize
  \/ \E w \in Workers :
       \/ Grant(w)
       \/ \E s \in Students : Admit(w, s) \/ Refuse(w, s)

SomeGrant == \E w \in Workers : Grant(w)
SomeHandle == \E w \in Workers, s \in Students : Admit(w, s) \/ Refuse(w, s)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SomeGrant)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeHandle)

EveryStudentEventuallyHandled ==
  \A s \in Students : (writer[s] = NoOne) ~> (writer[s] # NoOne)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {wkA, wkB}
    Students = {stu1, stu2}
    NoOne = nobody
    MaxGen = 2
    MaxSeats = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleWriter
PROPERTY EveryStudentEventuallyHandled
nl:
A university course-registration system lets several registration workers write
decisions into the enrollment book for one over-subscribed section. Only the
worker currently holding the section's lease may write, and the lease carries a
generation number. The section's seat capacity is edited by the registrar while
registration is running, so the number of seats can grow or shrink at any time.

Every decision written into the book is stamped with the writing worker and the
lease generation that was in force when it was written. When a lease expires the
generation advances, which retires every stamp that came before it.

Five things can happen. Grant: when no worker holds the lease, a worker takes
it. Expire: the lease held by a worker lapses, the section becomes unleased, and
the generation advances by one. Admit: the lease holder handles a student who
has no decision yet and there is still a free seat, giving the student a seat
and stamping the decision with itself and the current generation. Refuse: the
lease holder handles a student who has no decision yet when the seats already
taken have reached capacity, stamping a no-seat decision with itself and the
current generation. Resize: the registrar changes the seat capacity to a
different value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No decision in the book is stamped with a generation ahead of
the current one, every decision stamped with the current generation names the
worker that actually holds the lease right now, and every seated student has a
decision on record.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every student without a decision is eventually handled by a
lease holder.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m0p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Total, MaxVersion, MaxLimit, NoRead

VARIABLES version, warehouse, hopper, sold, readAt, limit

vars == <<version, warehouse, hopper, sold, readAt, limit>>

\* Cans loaded across the whole network, summed machine by machine.
RECURSIVE Loaded(_)
Loaded(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET m == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN hopper[m] + Loaded(S \ {m})

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
  /\ warehouse \in 0 .. Total
  /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0 .. Total]
  /\ sold \in 0 .. Total
  /\ readAt \in [Machines -> (0 .. MaxVersion) \cup {NoRead}]
  /\ limit \in 1 .. MaxLimit

\* Nothing is created and nothing is destroyed: every can is in the warehouse,
\* in some hopper, or already sold.
CansConserved == warehouse + Loaded(Machines) + sold = Total

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ warehouse = Total
  /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ sold = 0
  /\ readAt = [m \in Machines |-> NoRead]
  /\ limit \in 1 .. MaxLimit

Read(m) ==
  /\ readAt[m] = NoRead
  /\ warehouse > 0
  /\ readAt' = [readAt EXCEPT ![m] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, warehouse, hopper, sold, limit>>

\* The optimistic commit succeeds only if nobody moved the version meanwhile.
Commit(m) ==
  /\ readAt[m] = version
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ warehouse > 0
  /\ hopper[m] < limit
  /\ warehouse' = warehouse - 1
  /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] + 1]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ readAt' = [readAt EXCEPT ![m] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sold, limit>>

Retry(m) ==
  /\ readAt[m] # NoRead
  /\ readAt[m] # version
  /\ readAt' = [readAt EXCEPT ![m] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, warehouse, hopper, sold, limit>>

Sell(m) ==
  /\ hopper[m] > 0
  /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] - 1]
  /\ sold' = sold + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, warehouse, readAt, limit>>

\* Hopper capacity is re-rated by the operator while the network runs.
Rerate ==
  /\ \E c \in 1 .. MaxLimit : c # limit /\ limit' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, warehouse, hopper, sold, readAt>>

Next ==
  \/ Rerate
  \/ \E m \in Machines :
       \/ Read(m)
       \/ Commit(m)
       \/ Retry(m)
       \/ Sell(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vmA, vmB}
    Total = 3
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxLimit = 2
    NoRead = noRead
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CansConserved
nl:
A network of vending machines draws from one central warehouse record for a
single product line. Cans are never created and never destroyed: every can is
either sitting in the warehouse, loaded in some machine's hopper, or already
sold to a customer.

Machines do not lock the warehouse record. A machine reads the record together
with its version number, and later tries to commit a one-can transfer; the
commit is only accepted if the version has not moved since the read, and the
accepted commit bumps the version. If the version has moved, the machine throws
its read away and retries later. The operator also re-rates hopper capacity
while the network is running, so the per-machine hopper limit changes at
runtime.

Five things can happen. Read: a machine with no outstanding read takes the
current version number while the warehouse is non-empty. Commit: a machine
whose outstanding read still matches the live version, with the warehouse
non-empty and its hopper below the current limit, moves one can from the
warehouse into its hopper and bumps the version, clearing its read. Retry: a
machine whose outstanding read no longer matches the live version throws that
read away. Sell: a machine with at least one can in its hopper sells one can to
a customer. Rerate: the operator sets the hopper limit to a different value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The cans in the warehouse, the cans loaded in all machine
hoppers, and the cans already sold always add up to exactly the number of cans
the network started with.

---- MODULE W4Od4m4p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cars, LaneCap, NoCar

ASSUME NoCar \notin Cars

VARIABLES forecourt, lane, bay, record, overrideLeft

vars == <<forecourt, lane, bay, record, overrideLeft>>

InLane == {lane[i] : i \in 1 .. Len(lane)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ forecourt \subseteq Cars
  /\ Len(lane) <= LaneCap + 1
  /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(lane) : lane[i] \in Cars
  /\ bay \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
  /\ record \subseteq Cars
  /\ overrideLeft \in BOOLEAN

\* Every car sits in exactly one of the four places, so no car's write into the
\* shared wash record can go missing on the way.
NoCarLost ==
  /\ forecourt \cup InLane \cup record \cup (IF bay = NoCar THEN {} ELSE {bay}) = Cars
  /\ forecourt \cap InLane = {}
  /\ forecourt \cap record = {}
  /\ InLane \cap record = {}
  /\ bay \notin forecourt \cup InLane \cup record

Init ==
  /\ forecourt = Cars
  /\ lane = << >>
  /\ bay = NoCar
  /\ record = {}
  /\ overrideLeft = TRUE

\* Backpressure: the greeter stops admitting once the lane is at its limit.
Admit(c) ==
  /\ c \in forecourt
  /\ Len(lane) < LaneCap
  /\ lane' = Append(lane, c)
  /\ forecourt' = forecourt \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bay, record, overrideLeft>>

\* The manager's one-shot override pushes past the backpressure.
ForcePush(c) ==
  /\ c \in forecourt
  /\ overrideLeft
  /\ Len(lane) = LaneCap
  /\ lane' = Append(lane, c)
  /\ forecourt' = forecourt \ {c}
  /\ overrideLeft' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bay, record>>

Pull ==
  /\ lane # << >>
  /\ bay = NoCar
  /\ bay' = Head(lane)
  /\ lane' = Tail(lane)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<forecourt, record, overrideLeft>>

Finish ==
  /\ bay # NoCar
  /\ record' = record \cup {bay}
  /\ bay' = NoCar
  /\ UNCHANGED <<forecourt, lane, overrideLeft>>

\* A whole cohort only comes back round once every car has been written.
NewCycle ==
  /\ record = Cars
  /\ record' = {}
  /\ forecourt' = Cars
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lane, bay, overrideLeft>>

Next ==
  \/ Pull
  \/ Finish
  \/ NewCycle
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Admit(c) \/ ForcePush(c)

SomeAdmit == \E c \in Cars : Admit(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(SomeAdmit)
  /\ WF_vars(Pull)
  /\ WF_vars(Finish)

EveryWaitingCarIsRecorded ==
  \A c \in Cars : (c \in forecourt) ~> (c \in record)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    LaneCap = 1
    NoCar = noCar
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoCarLost
PROPERTY EveryWaitingCarIsRecorded
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line pulls cars out of a bounded intake lane. The lane holds
only so many cars; when it is full the greeter has to hold cars back on the
forecourt, which is the line's backpressure. One shared wash record is kept for
the site, and every car that leaves the forecourt has to end up written into
that record -- a car must never disappear between the forecourt, the lane, the
wash bay and the record.

The site manager holds one privileged override that can force a single car into
the lane past the backpressure, over the lane's normal limit. The override is
one-shot.

Five things can happen. Admit: the greeter moves a forecourt car onto the tail
of the lane while the lane is below its limit. ForcePush: the manager, with the
override still unused, forces a forecourt car onto the tail of a full lane and
burns the override. Pull: the conveyor takes the head car of the lane into the
empty wash bay. Finish: the car in the wash bay is washed and written into the
shared wash record, leaving the bay empty. NewCycle: once every car on site has
been written into the shared wash record, the whole cohort is cleared out of the
record and returned to the forecourt for another pass.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every car is accounted for in exactly one place -- on the
forecourt, in the intake lane, in the wash bay, or written into the shared wash
record -- so no car's update to the record is ever lost.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car waiting on the forecourt is eventually washed and
written into the shared wash record.

---- MODULE W4Od3m2p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Members, Window, MaxRounds

VARIABLES round, phase, ballot, held, settled, stopped

vars == <<round, phase, ballot, held, settled, stopped>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0 .. MaxRounds
  /\ phase \in {"closed", "voting"}
  /\ ballot \in [Members -> {"blank", "go", "stop"}]
  /\ held \in 0 .. Window
  /\ settled \in 0 .. Window
  /\ stopped \subseteq Members

AllGo == \A m \in Members : ballot[m] = "go"

\* The bounded liquidity window covers settled value and provisional holds
\* together, and nothing stays held once the round is closed.
WindowNotExceeded ==
  /\ settled + held <= Window
  /\ phase = "closed" => held = 0

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ phase = "closed"
  /\ ballot = [m \in Members |-> "blank"]
  /\ held = 0
  /\ settled = 0
  /\ stopped = {}

OpenRound ==
  /\ phase = "closed"
  /\ round < MaxRounds
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ phase' = "voting"
  /\ ballot' = [m \in Members |-> "blank"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<held, settled, stopped>>

\* A member may only vote to go ahead if its unit still fits in the window.
VoteGo(m) ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ m \notin stopped
  /\ ballot[m] = "blank"
  /\ settled + held + 1 <= Window
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = "go"]
  /\ held' = held + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, settled, stopped>>

VoteStop(m) ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ m \notin stopped
  /\ ballot[m] = "blank"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = "stop"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, held, settled, stopped>>

\* A member can stop dead without telling the house.
Fail(m) ==
  /\ m \notin stopped
  /\ stopped' = stopped \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, ballot, held, settled>>

Recover(m) ==
  /\ m \in stopped
  /\ stopped' = stopped \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, ballot, held, settled>>

CommitRound ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ AllGo
  /\ settled' = settled + held
  /\ held' = 0
  /\ phase' = "closed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, ballot, stopped>>

AbortRound ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ ~AllGo
  /\ held' = 0
  /\ phase' = "closed"
  /\ ballot' = [m \in Members |-> "blank"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, settled, stopped>>

Next ==
  \/ OpenRound
  \/ CommitRound
  \/ AbortRound
  \/ \E m \in Members :
       VoteGo(m) \/ VoteStop(m) \/ Fail(m) \/ Recover(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Members = {mbA, mbB}
    Window = 3
    MaxRounds = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WindowNotExceeded
nl:
A clearing house settles an interbank batch in rounds, and each round is driven
by a two-phase commit across the member banks. The house runs against a bounded
liquidity window: the value already settled today plus the value provisionally
held for the round in progress can never exceed the window size.

A round opens by asking every member to vote. A member that votes to go ahead
takes one unit of the window and holds it provisionally; a member may only vote
to go ahead if that extra unit still fits inside the window. When every member
has voted to go ahead, the house commits the round and the provisional holds
become settled value. Otherwise the house aborts and every provisional hold is
released. A member can stop dead without telling anyone, in which case it never
votes and the round is aborted by the house.

Seven things can happen. OpenRound: with no round in progress and rounds left in
the day, the house clears all votes and opens the voting phase. VoteGo: a live
member that has not voted yet votes to go ahead and takes one unit of the
window, provided the unit fits. VoteStop: a live member that has not voted yet
votes to stop. Fail: a member stops dead silently. Recover: a stopped member
comes back up. CommitRound: with every member having voted to go ahead, the
house turns the provisional holds into settled value and closes the round.
AbortRound: with the round in progress and not every member having voted to go
ahead, the house releases every provisional hold, clears the votes and closes
the round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The settled value plus the provisionally held value never
exceeds the liquidity window, and no value is left provisionally held once no
round is in progress.

---- MODULE W4Od4m5p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Lines, Controllers, Quorum, Charge, NoLine

ASSUME NoLine \notin Lines

VARIABLES reservoir, inHand, recovered, proposal, tally

vars == <<reservoir, inHand, recovered, proposal, tally>>

RECURSIVE Held(_)
Held(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN inHand[l] + Held(S \ {l})

TypeOK ==
  /\ reservoir \in 0 .. Charge
  /\ inHand \in [Lines -> 0 .. Charge]
  /\ recovered \in 0 .. Charge
  /\ proposal \in Lines \cup {NoLine}
  /\ tally \subseteq Controllers

\* Detergent is neither created nor destroyed, and a tally only exists while a
\* proposal is actually standing.
DetergentConserved ==
  /\ reservoir + Held(Lines) + recovered = Charge
  /\ proposal = NoLine => tally = {}

Init ==
  /\ reservoir = Charge
  /\ inHand = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
  /\ recovered = 0
  /\ proposal = NoLine
  /\ tally = {}

Propose(l) ==
  /\ proposal = NoLine
  /\ reservoir > 0
  /\ proposal' = l
  /\ tally' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, inHand, recovered>>

CastVote(c) ==
  /\ proposal # NoLine
  /\ c \notin tally
  /\ tally' = tally \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, inHand, recovered, proposal>>

\* Only a quorum can move a dose out of the shared reservoir.
Carry ==
  /\ proposal # NoLine
  /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
  /\ reservoir > 0
  /\ reservoir' = reservoir - 1
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![proposal] = inHand[proposal] + 1]
  /\ proposal' = NoLine
  /\ tally' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED recovered

Spray(l) ==
  /\ inHand[l] > 0
  /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![l] = inHand[l] - 1]
  /\ recovered' = recovered + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservoir, proposal, tally>>

Reclaim ==
  /\ recovered > 0
  /\ recovered' = recovered - 1
  /\ reservoir' = reservoir + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inHand, proposal, tally>>

Next ==
  \/ Carry
  \/ Reclaim
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : CastVote(c)
  \/ \E l \in Lines : Propose(l) \/ Spray(l)

SomeVote == \E c \in Controllers : CastVote(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SomeVote)
  /\ WF_vars(Carry)

EveryProposalIsCarried == (proposal # NoLine) ~> (proposal = NoLine)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Lines = {lnA, lnB}
    Controllers = {ctl1, ctl2, ctl3}
    Quorum = 2
    Charge = 2
    NoLine = noLine
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DetergentConserved
PROPERTY EveryProposalIsCarried
nl:
A car-wash site runs two independent conveyor lines that draw detergent from a
single shared reservoir. Detergent is never created and never destroyed: every
dose is either sitting in the reservoir, already handed to one of the lines and
not yet sprayed, or sprayed and sitting in the recovery tank.

No line may help itself. To take a dose, a line puts up a proposal, and the
site's controllers vote on it one at a time; the dose only moves once a quorum
of controllers has backed that proposal. A proposal is never withdrawn -- it
stays up until the quorum carries it.

Five things can happen. Propose: with no proposal on the table and detergent in
the reservoir, one of the lines puts up a proposal for one dose and the vote
tally starts empty. CastVote: a controller that has not yet backed the standing
proposal backs it. Carry: once the tally has reached quorum, one dose leaves the
reservoir and is handed to the proposing line, the proposal comes down and the
tally is cleared. Spray: a line with at least one dose in hand sprays it, moving
the dose to the recovery tank. Reclaim: one dose in the recovery tank is
filtered back into the shared reservoir.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The doses in the reservoir, the doses held by the two lines,
and the doses in the recovery tank always add up to the site's fixed detergent
charge, and no votes are on the tally when no proposal is standing.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal that goes up is eventually carried by a
quorum and taken down.

---- MODULE W4Od17m9p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Chutes, NoChute, MaxEpoch, MaxFlight

ASSUME NoChute \notin Chutes

Msgs == [bag : Bags, chute : Chutes, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

VARIABLES epoch, routed, confirmed, inflight, offline

vars == <<epoch, routed, confirmed, inflight, offline>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ routed \in [Bags -> Chutes \cup {NoChute}]
  /\ confirmed \subseteq Bags
  /\ inflight \subseteq Msgs
  /\ offline \subseteq Chutes

\* A confirmed bag must have a live entry, and that entry must never name a
\* chute the current layout has taken out of service.
NoLostRouting ==
  /\ \A b \in Bags : b \in confirmed => routed[b] # NoChute
  /\ \A b \in Bags : b \in confirmed => routed[b] \notin offline

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ routed = [b \in Bags |-> NoChute]
  /\ confirmed = {}
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ offline = {}

\* A reconfiguration may not strand a bag that is already committed.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E no \in SUBSET Chutes :
       /\ no # Chutes
       /\ no # offline
       /\ \A b \in confirmed : routed[b] \notin no
       /\ offline' = no
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<routed, confirmed, inflight>>

Post(b, c) ==
  /\ b \notin confirmed
  /\ routed[b] = NoChute
  /\ c \notin offline
  /\ Cardinality(inflight) < MaxFlight
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[bag |-> b, chute |-> c, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, routed, confirmed, offline>>

\* Any in-flight message may be picked up, in any order.
Apply(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.ep = epoch
  /\ m.chute \notin offline
  /\ routed[m.bag] = NoChute
  /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![m.bag] = m.chute]
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {m.bag}
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, offline>>

Discard(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ \/ m.ep # epoch
     \/ m.chute \in offline
     \/ routed[m.bag] # NoChute
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, routed, confirmed, offline>>

Unload(b) ==
  /\ b \in confirmed
  /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![b] = NoChute]
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inflight, offline>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E m \in Msgs : Apply(m) \/ Discard(m)
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Unload(b) \/ \E c \in Chutes : Post(b, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bags = {bg1, bg2}
    Chutes = {chA, chB}
    NoChute = noChute
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxFlight = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostRouting
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps one shared routing record that says, for each
bag, which chute it has been committed to. Check-in desks post assignment
messages to the router over a fabric that gives no ordering guarantee: two
messages posted in one order can arrive in the other order, or a duplicate can
arrive long after the bag was already committed.

The router publishes its chute layout under an epoch number. A reconfiguration
bumps the epoch and takes some chutes out of service, but it is never allowed to
retire a chute that a confirmed bag is already committed to, and at least one
chute always stays in service. Every assignment message carries the epoch it was
posted under, so a message that survives a reconfiguration is no longer valid.

Five things can happen. Reconfigure: the router bumps the epoch and installs a
new out-of-service set that leaves at least one chute live and retires no chute
that a confirmed bag is committed to. Post: a desk posts an assignment message
naming an uncommitted bag and an in-service chute, stamped with the current
epoch. Apply: the router picks any in-flight message whose stamp is the current
epoch, whose chute is still in service, and whose bag is still uncommitted, and
commits that bag to that chute in the shared record, confirming it to the desk
and consuming the message. Discard: the router throws away any in-flight message
whose stamp is stale, or whose chute has been retired, or whose bag is already
committed. Unload: a confirmed bag is taken off its chute, clearing its entry in
the shared record and its confirmation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every confirmed bag has a live entry in the shared routing
record, and that entry never names a chute that has been taken out of service,
so no confirmed routing update is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od7m9p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Bays, Boxes, NoBox, InAir, MaxEpoch

ASSUME NoBox \notin Boxes
ASSUME InAir \notin Bays

VARIABLES epoch, plan, copyEp, spreader, standing

vars == <<epoch, plan, copyEp, spreader, standing>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ plan \in [Cranes -> Bays]
  /\ copyEp \in [Cranes -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
  /\ spreader \in [Cranes -> Boxes \cup {NoBox}]
  /\ standing \in [Boxes -> Bays \cup {InAir}]

Idle == \A c \in Cranes : spreader[c] = NoBox

\* A crane on a superseded plan copy is not authorised to touch cargo, and the
\* spreader map and the yard map must tell the same story about every box.
NoStaleCraneWork ==
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : spreader[c] # NoBox => copyEp[c] = epoch
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : spreader[c] # NoBox => standing[spreader[c]] = InAir
  /\ \A k \in Boxes : standing[k] = InAir => \E c \in Cranes : spreader[c] = k

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ plan \in [Cranes -> Bays]
  /\ copyEp = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
  /\ spreader = [c \in Cranes |-> NoBox]
  /\ standing \in [Boxes -> Bays]

\* The office only republishes while every spreader is empty.
Republish ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ Idle
  /\ \E np \in [Cranes -> Bays] :
       /\ np # plan
       /\ plan' = np
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<copyEp, spreader, standing>>

\* A slow crane catches up with the published plan.
Refresh(c) ==
  /\ copyEp[c] < epoch
  /\ copyEp' = [copyEp EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, plan, spreader, standing>>

Lift(c, k) ==
  /\ copyEp[c] = epoch
  /\ spreader[c] = NoBox
  /\ standing[k] = plan[c]
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![k] = InAir]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, plan, copyEp>>

Land(c) ==
  /\ spreader[c] # NoBox
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![spreader[c]] = plan[c]]
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = NoBox]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, plan, copyEp>>

Shuffle(k, b) ==
  /\ standing[k] # InAir
  /\ standing[k] # b
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![k] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, plan, copyEp, spreader>>

Next ==
  \/ Republish
  \/ \E c \in Cranes :
       \/ Refresh(c)
       \/ Land(c)
       \/ \E k \in Boxes : Lift(c, k)
  \/ \E k \in Boxes, b \in Bays : Shuffle(k, b)

SomeRefresh == \E c \in Cranes : Refresh(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SomeRefresh)

EverySlowCraneCatchesUp ==
  \A c \in Cranes : (copyEp[c] < epoch) ~> (copyEp[c] = epoch)

====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard works to a yard plan that assigns each gantry crane
one bay to work. The plan is published under an epoch number, and each crane
carries its own copy of the plan together with the epoch that copy came from. A
crane is never taken out of service and never fails, but it can be slow: it may
sit on a superseded copy of the plan for a long time before it picks up the new
one. A crane running on a superseded copy is not authorised to touch cargo.

Five things can happen. Republish: with no crane in the middle of a lift, the
yard office bumps the epoch and installs a different bay assignment. Refresh: a
crane whose copy is behind the published epoch picks up the current plan and its
epoch. Lift: a crane whose copy is current, with its spreader empty, hoists a
container that is standing in the bay its current plan assigns it, so the
container is in the air under that crane. Land: a crane holding a container sets
it down in the bay its current plan assigns it, freeing the spreader. Shuffle: a
yard truck drags a container that is standing on the ground from its bay to a
different bay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Only a crane whose plan copy matches the published epoch is
ever holding a container, every held container is recorded as being in the air,
and every container recorded as being in the air is held by exactly the crane
that lifted it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every crane sitting on a superseded copy of the plan
eventually picks up the published one.

---- MODULE W4Od4m6p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Attendants, Cars, NoOne, MaxGen, LinkCap

ASSUME NoOne \notin Attendants

Notes == [car : Cars, by : Attendants, g : 0 .. MaxGen]

VARIABLES lease, gen, inflight, record, promised

vars == <<lease, gen, inflight, record, promised>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lease \in Attendants \cup {NoOne}
  /\ gen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ inflight \subseteq Notes
  /\ record \in [Cars -> Attendants \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ promised \subseteq Cars

\* A promise never evaporates: it is either honoured in the shared record or
\* still represented by a message that has not been picked up yet.
NoSignOffLost ==
  /\ \A c \in Cars :
       c \in promised => (record[c] # NoOne \/ \E m \in inflight : m.car = c)
  /\ \A c \in Cars : record[c] # NoOne => c \in promised

Init ==
  /\ lease = NoOne
  /\ gen = 0
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ record = [c \in Cars |-> NoOne]
  /\ promised = {}

Grant(a) ==
  /\ lease = NoOne
  /\ lease' = a
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, inflight, record, promised>>

\* Expiry advances the generation, retiring everything still in flight.
Expire ==
  /\ lease # NoOne
  /\ gen < MaxGen
  /\ lease' = NoOne
  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, record, promised>>

Post(a, c) ==
  /\ lease = a
  /\ c \notin promised
  /\ record[c] = NoOne
  /\ Cardinality(inflight) < LinkCap
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[car |-> c, by |-> a, g |-> gen]}
  /\ promised' = promised \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, gen, record>>

\* The clerk may pick messages up in any order.
Accept(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.g = gen
  /\ lease = m.by
  /\ record[m.car] = NoOne
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![m.car] = m.by]
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, gen, promised>>

Refuse(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ \/ m.g # gen
     \/ lease # m.by
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ promised' = promised \ {m.car}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, gen, record>>

Archive(c) ==
  /\ record[c] # NoOne
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![c] = NoOne]
  /\ promised' = promised \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, gen, inflight>>

Next ==
  \/ Expire
  \/ \E m \in Notes : Accept(m) \/ Refuse(m)
  \/ \E a \in Attendants : Grant(a) \/ \E c \in Cars : Post(a, c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Archive(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Attendants = {atA, atB}
    Cars = {cw1, cw2}
    NoOne = nobody
    MaxGen = 2
    LinkCap = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoSignOffLost
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line keeps one shared service record that says, for each
car, which attendant signed off its wash. Only the attendant currently holding
the site lease may write into that record. The lease has an expiry: when it
lapses the site's lease generation advances, which retires every write that was
issued under the old generation.

Attendants do not write the record directly. They post a sign-off message
stamped with themselves and the generation in force, and the record clerk picks
messages up over a link that gives no ordering guarantee, so messages may be
picked up in any order. Posting a sign-off also puts the car on the promised
list, and the site's rule is that a promised car is either already in the shared
record or still has its message in flight -- a promise must never evaporate.

Six things can happen. Grant: with the lease free, an attendant takes it.
Expire: the held lease lapses, leaving the lease free and advancing the
generation. Post: the lease holder puts a car that is neither promised nor
recorded on the promised list and posts a sign-off message stamped with itself
and the current generation, as long as the link is not already saturated.
Accept: the clerk picks up any in-flight message whose generation is still
current and whose attendant still holds the lease, and writes that car into the
shared record. Refuse: the clerk picks up any in-flight message whose generation
is stale or whose attendant no longer holds the lease, drops it, and takes the
car back off the promised list. Archive: a car already written into the shared
record is archived at the end of the shift, clearing its record entry and its
promise.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every promised car is either already written into the shared
service record or still has its sign-off message in flight, and every car in the
record is on the promised list, so no sign-off is ever lost.

CONSTANTS Flights, NumPositions, Occupancy

Positions == 1 .. NumPositions

Step(p) == IF p = NumPositions THEN 1 ELSE p + 1

VARIABLES token, sector, waiting, outstanding, onRunway, done

vars == <<token, sector, waiting, outstanding, onRunway, done>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Positions
  /\ sector \in [Flights -> Positions]
  /\ waiting \subseteq Flights
  /\ outstanding \subseteq Flights
  /\ onRunway \subseteq Flights
  /\ done \subseteq Flights

\* An issued-but-unread clearance still counts against the occupancy bound,
\* because the link may deliver clearances in any order.
RunwayBoundHeld ==
  /\ Cardinality(onRunway \cup outstanding) <= Occupancy
  /\ onRunway \cap outstanding = {}

Init ==
  /\ token \in Positions
  /\ sector \in [Flights -> Positions]
  /\ waiting = Flights
  /\ outstanding = {}
  /\ onRunway = {}
  /\ done = {}

PassToken ==
  /\ token' = Step(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, waiting, outstanding, onRunway, done>>

\* Only the token holder may issue, and only for its own sector's flights.
Issue(f) ==
  /\ f \in waiting
  /\ sector[f] = token
  /\ Cardinality(onRunway \cup outstanding) < Occupancy
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {f}
  /\ outstanding' = outstanding \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sector, onRunway, done>>

ReadBack(f) ==
  /\ f \in outstanding
  /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {f}
  /\ onRunway' = onRunway \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sector, waiting, done>>

Vacate(f) ==
  /\ f \in onRunway
  /\ onRunway' = onRunway \ {f}
  /\ done' = done \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sector, waiting, outstanding>>

\* A whole wave only restarts once every flight in it has rolled clear.
NewWave ==
  /\ done = Flights
  /\ done' = {}
  /\ waiting' = Flights
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, sector, outstanding, onRunway>>

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ NewWave
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Issue(f) \/ ReadBack(f) \/ Vacate(f)

SomeIssue == \E f \in Flights : Issue(f)
SomeReadBack == \E f \in Flights : ReadBack(f)
SomeVacate == \E f \in Flights : Vacate(f)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeIssue)
  /\ WF_vars(SomeReadBack)
  /\ WF_vars(SomeVacate)

  \A f \in Flights : (f \in waiting) ~> (f \in done)

CONSTANTS
    Flights = {fl1, fl2}
    NumPositions = 2
    Occupancy = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT RunwayBoundHeld
PROPERTY EveryFlightRollsClear
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator serves several tower positions, each of which
owns the inbound flights for its own sector. Only one position at a time may
issue clearances: a single token walks a fixed ring of positions, and a position
may only issue a clearance while it holds the token.

The runway complex has a hard occupancy bound. A clearance that has been issued
but not yet read back by the flight deck still counts against that bound,
because the clearance link gives no ordering guarantee: two clearances issued in
one order may be read back in the other order, so the allocator can never assume
an issued clearance has not landed yet.

Five things can happen. PassToken: the token moves one step around the ring of
positions. Issue: the position holding the token takes one of its own waiting
flights and issues a clearance for it, provided the outstanding clearances plus
the aircraft already on the runway are still below the occupancy bound. ReadBack:
any outstanding clearance, in any order, is read back by its flight deck and the
aircraft moves onto the runway. Vacate: an aircraft on the runway rolls clear of
the complex and is done. NewWave: once every flight in the wave is done, the
whole wave is reset and all flights go back to waiting at their own sector
positions.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The aircraft on the runway together with the clearances still
outstanding never exceed the occupancy bound, and no flight is ever both on the
runway and holding an outstanding clearance.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every waiting flight is eventually cleared, lands, and rolls
clear of the runway complex.

---- MODULE W4Od0m3p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Changes, NoNode, MaxTerm

ASSUME NoNode \notin Nodes

Majorities == {Q \in SUBSET Nodes : 2 * Cardinality(Q) > Cardinality(Nodes)}

VARIABLES leader, term, copy, confirmed, stopped

vars == <<leader, term, copy, confirmed, stopped>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ copy \in [Nodes -> SUBSET Changes]
  /\ confirmed \subseteq Changes
  /\ stopped \subseteq Nodes

Carriers(ch) == {n \in Nodes : ch \in copy[n]}

\* A confirmed booking change survives every failover: the sitting leader still
\* carries it and a majority of nodes still carry it.
NoConfirmedChangeLost ==
  /\ leader # NoNode => confirmed \subseteq copy[leader]
  /\ \A ch \in confirmed : Carriers(ch) \in Majorities

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoNode
  /\ term = 0
  /\ copy = [n \in Nodes |-> {}]
  /\ confirmed = {}
  /\ stopped = {}

\* Only a node that covers some whole majority may take the day-sheet.
Elect(n) ==
  /\ n \notin stopped
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader # n
  /\ \E Q \in Majorities : \A m \in Q : copy[m] \subseteq copy[n]
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, confirmed, stopped>>

Crash(n) ==
  /\ n \notin stopped
  /\ stopped' = stopped \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, copy, confirmed>>

Restart(n) ==
  /\ n \in stopped
  /\ stopped' = stopped \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, copy, confirmed>>

Draft(ch) ==
  /\ leader # NoNode
  /\ leader \notin stopped
  /\ ch \notin copy[leader]
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![leader] = copy[leader] \cup {ch}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, confirmed, stopped>>

Push(n, ch) ==
  /\ leader # NoNode
  /\ leader \notin stopped
  /\ n # leader
  /\ n \notin stopped
  /\ ch \in copy[leader]
  /\ ch \notin copy[n]
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = copy[n] \cup {ch}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, confirmed, stopped>>

Confirm(ch) ==
  /\ leader # NoNode
  /\ ch \in copy[leader]
  /\ Carriers(ch) \in Majorities
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {ch}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, copy, stopped>>

\* A stopped node loses work that was never confirmed.
Scrub(n, ch) ==
  /\ n \in stopped
  /\ ch \in copy[n]
  /\ ch \notin confirmed
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = copy[n] \ {ch}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, confirmed, stopped>>

Next ==
  \/ \E ch \in Changes : Draft(ch) \/ Confirm(ch)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes :
       \/ Elect(n) \/ Crash(n) \/ Restart(n)
       \/ \E ch \in Changes : Push(n, ch) \/ Scrub(n, ch)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {schA, schB, schC}
    Changes = {bk1, bk2}
    NoNode = noNode
    MaxTerm = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoConfirmedChangeLost
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps the theatre day-sheet replicated on
several scheduler nodes. One node is elected to lead; only the leader may write
a new booking change, and it then pushes that change out to the other nodes. A
node can crash silently -- it simply stops answering, with no announcement --
and when it comes back it may have lost work it had not yet had confirmed.

A change is confirmed to the surgeon only once a majority of nodes are carrying
it and the leader is carrying it too. Leadership can only be taken by a live
node that is at least as up to date as every node in some majority, which is
what stops a confirmed booking change from being dropped on the floor by a
failover.

Seven things can happen. Elect: a live node whose copy of the day-sheet covers
the copies of every node in some majority takes leadership under the next term.
Crash: a node stops silently. Restart: a stopped node comes back up. Draft: the
live leader writes a booking change it does not yet carry into its own copy.
Push: the leader hands a change it carries to another live node that does not
carry it. Confirm: the leader confirms a change to the surgeon once the leader
carries it and a majority of nodes carry it. Scrub: a stopped node throws away a
change it carries that was never confirmed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every confirmed booking change is still carried by the current
leader and is still carried by a majority of nodes, so no confirmed update to
the shared day-sheet is ever lost across a failover.

---- MODULE W4Od9m9p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Instances, Feeders, NoOne, MaxEpoch

ASSUME NoOne \notin Instances

VARIABLES epoch, myEp, breaker, actuating, line, shedSet

vars == <<epoch, myEp, breaker, actuating, line, shedSet>>

Queued == {line[k] : k \in 1 .. Len(line)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ myEp \in [Instances -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
  /\ breaker \in Instances \cup {NoOne}
  /\ actuating \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ \A k \in 1 .. Len(line) : line[k] \in Instances
  /\ shedSet \subseteq Feeders

\* The breaker is a single critical resource: whoever is actuating must be the
\* instance it was handed to, and must be on the published epoch.
BreakerHeldAlone ==
  /\ \A i \in Instances : actuating[i] => breaker = i
  /\ \A i \in Instances : actuating[i] => myEp[i] = epoch
  /\ breaker # NoOne => actuating[breaker]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ myEp = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
  /\ breaker = NoOne
  /\ actuating = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ line = << >>
  /\ shedSet = {}

Republish ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ breaker = NoOne
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<myEp, breaker, actuating, line, shedSet>>

Sync(i) ==
  /\ myEp[i] < epoch
  /\ myEp' = [myEp EXCEPT ![i] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, breaker, actuating, line, shedSet>>

Enqueue(i) ==
  /\ ~actuating[i]
  /\ i \notin Queued
  /\ line' = Append(line, i)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEp, breaker, actuating, shedSet>>

\* First in the line, first served -- and only on the published epoch.
Acquire ==
  /\ line # << >>
  /\ breaker = NoOne
  /\ myEp[Head(line)] = epoch
  /\ breaker' = Head(line)
  /\ actuating' = [actuating EXCEPT ![Head(line)] = TRUE]
  /\ line' = Tail(line)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEp, shedSet>>

Shed(i, f) ==
  /\ actuating[i]
  /\ f \notin shedSet
  /\ shedSet' = shedSet \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEp, breaker, actuating, line>>

Release(i) ==
  /\ actuating[i]
  /\ actuating' = [actuating EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ breaker' = NoOne
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEp, line, shedSet>>

Restore(f) ==
  /\ f \in shedSet
  /\ shedSet' = shedSet \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, myEp, breaker, actuating, line>>

Next ==
  \/ Republish
  \/ Acquire
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : Restore(f)
  \/ \E i \in Instances :
       \/ Sync(i) \/ Enqueue(i) \/ Release(i)
       \/ \E f \in Feeders : Shed(i, f)

SomeSync == \E i \in Instances : Sync(i)
SomeRelease == \E i \in Instances : Release(i)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SomeSync)
  /\ WF_vars(Acquire)
  /\ WF_vars(SomeRelease)

EveryQueuedInstanceActuates ==
  \A i \in Instances : (i \in Queued) ~> actuating[i]

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {ldA, ldB}
    Feeders = {fdr1, fdr2}
    NoOne = noOne
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BreakerHeldAlone
PROPERTY EveryQueuedInstanceActuates
nl:
A power-grid load shedder is run as two independent controller instances that
share one pool of feeders. Both instances can compute a shedding plan, but the
shed breaker itself is a single critical piece of switchgear: at any moment at
most one instance may be actuating it, and the instance that is actuating it
must be the one the breaker has actually been handed to.

The grid operator republishes the protection settings under an epoch number.
Each instance keeps its own copy of the epoch, and the breaker is only handed to
an instance whose copy matches the published epoch, so an instance running on
superseded settings can never actuate. The operator only republishes while the
breaker is free.

Seven things can happen. Republish: with the breaker free and epochs left, the
operator bumps the published epoch. Sync: an instance whose epoch copy is behind
picks up the published epoch. Enqueue: an instance that is not actuating and is
not already in the waiting line joins the back of the line. Acquire: when the
breaker is free and the instance at the front of the line has a current epoch
copy, the breaker is handed to it, it starts actuating, and it leaves the line.
Shed: the instance that is actuating opens one feeder that is not already shed.
Release: an actuating instance stops actuating and the breaker goes free.
Restore: a shed feeder is closed again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any instance that is actuating is exactly the instance the
breaker has been handed to, and it is running on the published epoch, so the
breaker is never actuated by two instances at once nor by a superseded one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instance that joins the waiting line eventually gets
the breaker and starts actuating.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, NoCrane

ASSUME NoCrane \notin Cranes

VARIABLES phase, candidate, ballot, granted, standing, override

vars == <<phase, candidate, ballot, granted, standing, override>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "prepare"}
  /\ candidate \in Cranes \cup {NoCrane}
  /\ ballot \in [Cranes -> {"blank", "yield", "refuse"}]
  /\ granted \in Cranes \cup {NoCrane}
  /\ standing \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

Blank == [c \in Cranes |-> "blank"]

AllYielded == \A c \in Cranes : c # candidate => ballot[c] = "yield"

\* The quay-rail segment is a single critical resource: the crane standing on
\* it is exactly the grantee, and no vote runs while it is occupied.
SegmentHeldAlone ==
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : standing[c] => granted = c
  /\ granted # NoCrane => standing[granted]
  /\ phase = "prepare" => granted = NoCrane

Init ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ candidate = NoCrane
  /\ ballot = Blank
  /\ granted = NoCrane
  /\ standing = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
  /\ override = FALSE

Begin(c) ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ granted = NoCrane
  /\ ~override
  /\ phase' = "prepare"
  /\ candidate' = c
  /\ ballot' = Blank
  /\ UNCHANGED <<granted, standing, override>>

Yield(c) ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ c # candidate
  /\ ballot[c] = "blank"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = "yield"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, candidate, granted, standing, override>>

Refuse(c) ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ c # candidate
  /\ ballot[c] = "blank"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = "refuse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, candidate, granted, standing, override>>

CommitGrant ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ AllYielded
  /\ granted = NoCrane
  /\ granted' = candidate
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![candidate] = TRUE]
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ candidate' = NoCrane
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, override>>

AbortGrant ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ \E c \in Cranes : c # candidate /\ ballot[c] = "refuse"
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ candidate' = NoCrane
  /\ ballot' = Blank
  /\ UNCHANGED <<granted, standing, override>>

RollOff(c) ==
  /\ standing[c]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ granted' = NoCrane
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, candidate, ballot, override>>

\* The harbour master outranks the whole vote.
MasterGrant(c) ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ granted = NoCrane
  /\ override' = TRUE
  /\ granted' = c
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ candidate' = NoCrane
  /\ ballot' = Blank

MasterStandDown ==
  /\ override
  /\ granted = NoCrane
  /\ override' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, candidate, ballot, granted, standing>>

Next ==
  \/ CommitGrant
  \/ AbortGrant
  \/ MasterStandDown
  \/ \E c \in Cranes :
       Begin(c) \/ Yield(c) \/ Refuse(c) \/ RollOff(c) \/ MasterGrant(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {gcA, gcB, gcC}
    NoCrane = noCrane
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SegmentHeldAlone
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has one shared quay-rail segment that runs past the
berth. The segment is a critical resource: exactly one gantry crane at a time
may be standing on it, and a crane standing on it must be the crane the segment
was actually granted to.

A crane cannot simply roll on. It asks the yard office to run a two-phase grant:
the office opens a prepare round naming the candidate, every other crane votes
either to yield the segment or to refuse, and the grant is only committed if
every other crane yielded. The harbour master holds a privileged override that
can hand the segment straight to a crane without any vote at all.

Eight things can happen. Begin: with no round running, the segment free and no
override in force, the office opens a prepare round for a candidate crane and
clears the votes. Yield: a crane other than the candidate votes to yield.
Refuse: a crane other than the candidate votes to refuse. CommitGrant: with
every other crane having yielded and the segment still free, the office grants
the segment to the candidate, which rolls onto it, and the round closes.
AbortGrant: with some other crane having refused, the office closes the round
and clears the votes, granting nothing. RollOff: the crane standing on the
segment rolls off and the segment goes free. MasterGrant: with no override in
force and the segment free, the harbour master engages the override, hands the
segment to a crane which rolls straight on, and closes any round in progress.
MasterStandDown: with the override in force and the segment free, the harbour
master disengages it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crane standing on the quay-rail segment is exactly the
crane the segment was granted to, the granted crane is always the one standing
on it, and no prepare round is ever running while the segment is occupied.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, MaxEpoch, MaxLimit

VARIABLES epoch, limit, queue, presses, printed, startEp

vars == <<epoch, limit, queue, presses, printed, startEp>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ limit \in 1 .. MaxLimit
  /\ queue \subseteq Jobs
  /\ presses \subseteq Jobs
  /\ printed \subseteq Jobs
  /\ startEp \in [Jobs -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

\* Printing is irreversible, so the printed pile is sealed off from the rest of
\* the shop: every job sits in exactly one of the three places.
PrintedNeverReprinted ==
  /\ queue \cup presses \cup printed = Jobs
  /\ printed \cap (queue \cup presses) = {}
  /\ queue \cap presses = {}

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ limit \in 1 .. MaxLimit
  /\ queue = Jobs
  /\ presses = {}
  /\ printed = {}
  /\ startEp = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]

Republish ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ \E c \in 1 .. MaxLimit : limit' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, presses, printed, startEp>>

\* Concurrency is re-rated without disturbing the epoch.
Rerate ==
  /\ \E c \in 1 .. MaxLimit : c # limit /\ limit' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, queue, presses, printed, startEp>>

Start(j) ==
  /\ j \in queue
  /\ Cardinality(presses) < limit
  /\ queue' = queue \ {j}
  /\ presses' = presses \cup {j}
  /\ startEp' = [startEp EXCEPT ![j] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, printed>>

Finish(j) ==
  /\ j \in presses
  /\ startEp[j] = epoch
  /\ presses' = presses \ {j}
  /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, queue, startEp>>

Abandon(j) ==
  /\ j \in presses
  /\ startEp[j] # epoch
  /\ presses' = presses \ {j}
  /\ queue' = queue \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, printed, startEp>>

  \/ Republish
  \/ Rerate
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Start(j) \/ Finish(j) \/ Abandon(j)

SomeFinish == \E j \in Jobs : Finish(j)

  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(SomeStart)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeFinish)
  /\ WF_vars(SomeAbandon)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Jobs = {jb1, jb2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxLimit = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PrintedNeverReprinted
PROPERTY EveryQueuedJobIsPrinted
nl:
A print shop spools jobs onto its presses. Putting a job onto paper is
irreversible: once the stock is printed there is no undoing it, so no job may
ever be printed twice.

The shop republishes its press layout under an epoch number, and it also
re-rates how many jobs may sit on the presses at once while the shop is running,
so the concurrency limit changes at runtime. Every job that goes onto a press is
stamped with the epoch it started under. A job whose stamp has been superseded
by a republish cannot be committed to paper -- the operator has to pull it back
into the queue and start it again under the current layout.

Five things can happen. Republish: with epochs left, the shop bumps the epoch
and installs a new concurrency limit. Rerate: the shop changes the concurrency
limit without touching the epoch. Start: a queued job moves onto a press while
the number of jobs on the presses is below the limit, and it is stamped with the
current epoch. Finish: a job on a press whose stamp is the current epoch is
committed to paper and moves into the printed pile. Abandon: a job on a press
whose stamp has been superseded is pulled off and put back in the queue.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job is in exactly one of the three places -- the queue,
the presses, or the printed pile -- so a job that has already been printed can
never be back in the queue or on a press, and can never be printed a second
time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every queued job is eventually committed to paper.

---- MODULE W4Od10m0p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, MaxVersion, MaxLimit, NoRead

VARIABLES version, atSignal, inSection, released, readAt, sectLimit

vars == <<version, atSignal, inSection, released, readAt, sectLimit>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
  /\ atSignal \subseteq Trains
  /\ inSection \subseteq Trains
  /\ released \subseteq Trains
  /\ readAt \in [Trains -> (0 .. MaxVersion) \cup {NoRead}]
  /\ sectLimit \in 1 .. MaxLimit

\* A release is irreversible, so a released train is off the holding signal for
\* good and can never be carrying an outstanding read to commit again.
ReleasedOnlyOnce ==
  /\ inSection \subseteq released
  /\ atSignal \cap released = {}
  /\ \A t \in Trains : t \in released => readAt[t] = NoRead

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ atSignal = Trains
  /\ inSection = {}
  /\ released = {}
  /\ readAt = [t \in Trains |-> NoRead]
  /\ sectLimit \in 1 .. MaxLimit

Read(t) ==
  /\ t \in atSignal
  /\ readAt[t] = NoRead
  /\ readAt' = [readAt EXCEPT ![t] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, atSignal, inSection, released, sectLimit>>

\* The optimistic commit is refused if anybody moved the table meanwhile.
Commit(t) ==
  /\ t \in atSignal
  /\ readAt[t] = version
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ Cardinality(inSection) < sectLimit
  /\ atSignal' = atSignal \ {t}
  /\ inSection' = inSection \cup {t}
  /\ released' = released \cup {t}
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ readAt' = [readAt EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED sectLimit

Retry(t) ==
  /\ readAt[t] # NoRead
  /\ readAt[t] # version
  /\ readAt' = [readAt EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, atSignal, inSection, released, sectLimit>>

Exit(t) ==
  /\ t \in inSection

CONSTANTS
    Trains = {tr1, tr2}
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxLimit = 2
    NoRead = noRead
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ReleasedOnlyOnce
nl:
A subway signalling system controls one running section made up of track blocks.
Releasing a train past the holding signal into the section is irreversible: once
the movement authority is issued the train is rolling and there is no way to
un-issue it, so a train must never be released a second time.

The signalling desks do not take a lock on the occupancy table. A desk reads the
table together with its version number and later tries to commit an authority;
the commit is only accepted if the version has not moved since the read, and an
accepted commit bumps the version. If the version has moved, the desk throws its
read away and retries. The control centre also re-rates how many trains may be
inside the section at once while service is running, so the section limit
changes at runtime.

Five things can happen. Read: a train standing at the holding signal with no
outstanding read takes the current version number. Commit: a train whose
outstanding read still matches the live version is released into the section,
provided the trains already inside are below the section limit; the train's
release is recorded permanently, the version is bumped and its read is cleared.
Retry: a train whose outstanding read no longer matches the live version throws
that read away. Exit: a train inside the section runs out the far end and leaves
the section, though its release stays on the permanent record. Rerate: the
control centre sets the section limit to a different value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every train inside the section has been released, no released
train is ever standing at the holding signal again, and no released train ever
holds an outstanding read -- so no train can be released twice.

  /\ ttl = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ lowStock = Machines
  /\ restocked = {}

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vmX, vmY}
    Vans = {vnA, vnB}
    NoVan = noVan
    MaxCrew = 2
    FullTtl = 2

INVARIANT LeasesWithinCrew
PROPERTY EveryLeaseIsGivenUp
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked by a fleet of vans. Before a van may
touch a machine it must take a restock lease on it, and the lease carries a
countdown: the lease ticks down and, when the countdown runs out, it lapses and
the machine goes back to being unleased whether or not the van got there.

The depot has a bounded crew: only so many machines may be under lease at the
same moment. That crew size is re-rated during the day, but the depot will only
re-rate down to a size that still covers the leases already out.

Five things can happen. Take: a van takes a lease on a machine that is running
low and is not already leased, provided the leases already out are below the
crew size; the countdown starts at full. Clock: while at least one lease is out,
the depot clock ticks every live lease down by one at once, and any lease that
was on its last tick lapses on the spot, going back to unleased with a zero
countdown. Fill: the van holding a live lease on a machine
restocks it, which clears the low-stock flag, releases the lease and zeroes the
countdown. Drain: a restocked machine sells out and goes back to running low.
Rerate: the depot changes the crew size to a different value that still covers
the leases currently out.

every leased machine has a countdown still running, and every unleased machine
has a zero countdown.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every lease that is taken out is eventually given up, either
because the machine was restocked or because the countdown lapsed.

CONSTANTS Loaders, LoopCap, PierCap, MaxTag, NoSnap

VARIABLES count, tag, seenCount, seenTag, pier

vars == <<count, tag, seenCount, seenTag, pier>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ count \in 0 .. LoopCap
  /\ tag \in 0 .. MaxTag
  /\ seenCount \in [Loaders -> 0 .. LoopCap]
  /\ seenTag \in [Loaders -> (0 .. MaxTag) \cup {NoSnap}]
  /\ pier \in 0 .. PierCap

\* The tag is a true version stamp: a snapshot whose tag still matches must
\* still describe the live count, which is what keeps the loop under capacity.
LoopWithinCapacity ==
  /\ count <= LoopCap
  /\ \A l \in Loaders : seenTag[l] = tag => seenCount[l] = count

Init ==
  /\ count = 0
  /\ tag = 0
  /\ seenCount = [l \in Loaders |-> 0]
  /\ seenTag = [l \in Loaders |-> NoSnap]
  /\ pier = 0

Arrive ==
  /\ pier < PierCap
  /\ pier' = pier + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, tag, seenCount, seenTag>>

Depart ==
  /\ pier > 0
  /\ pier' = pier - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, tag, seenCount, seenTag>>

Snapshot(l) ==
  /\ seenTag[l] = NoSnap
  /\ seenCount' = [seenCount EXCEPT ![l] = count]
  /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![l] = tag]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, tag, pier>>

\* The compare-and-swap only lands while the snapshotted tag is still live.
Push(l) ==
  /\ seenTag[l] = tag
  /\ seenCount[l] < LoopCap
  /\ pier > 0
  /\ tag < MaxTag
  /\ count' = seenCount[l] + 1
  /\ tag' = tag + 1
  /\ pier' = pier - 1
  /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![l] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED seenCount

\* A slow loader's stale snapshot is refused outright.
Reject(l) ==
  /\ seenTag[l] # NoSnap
  /\ seenTag[l] # tag
  /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![l] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, tag, seenCount, pier>>

Unload ==
  /\ count > 0
  /\ tag < MaxTag
  /\ count' = count - 1
  /\ tag' = tag + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seenCount, seenTag, pier>>

Next ==
  \/ Arrive
  \/ Depart
  \/ Unload
  \/ \E l \in Loaders : Snapshot(l) \/ Push(l) \/ Reject(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Loaders = {ldA, ldB}
    LoopCap = 2
    PierCap = 2
    MaxTag = 4
    NoSnap = noSnap
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LoopWithinCapacity
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags from an input pier onto a sorter loop. The
loop has a hard bag capacity that must never be exceeded. The loop's bag count
is published in a single register that also carries a tag, and the tag is bumped
by every write, so the tag identifies the exact version of the count.

Loaders never write the register blind. A loader takes a snapshot of the count
and the tag, decides against its own snapshot whether another bag fits, and then
tries a compare-and-swap: the write only lands if the live tag is still the tag
it snapshotted. A loader is never out of service, but it can be slow, so a
snapshot may be very old by the time the loader gets round to using it; such a
compare-and-swap is rejected and the snapshot is thrown away.

Six things can happen. Arrive: another bag joins the input pier, up to the
pier's limit. Depart: a bag on the pier is taken away by hand. Snapshot: a
loader with no snapshot in hand records the current count and tag. Push: a
loader whose snapshot tag still matches the live tag, whose snapshotted count is
below the loop capacity, and which has a bag on the pier, writes the snapshotted
count plus one into the register, bumps the tag, takes the bag off the pier and
drops its snapshot. Reject: a loader whose snapshot tag no longer matches the
live tag throws the snapshot away. Unload: a bag leaves the loop down a chute,
which decrements the register and bumps the tag.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The published loop count never exceeds the loop capacity, and
any loader whose snapshot tag still matches the live tag has a snapshotted count
that still matches the live count.

CONSTANTS Machines, Controllers, Quorum, NoMach
