vars == <<doorOpen, canister, petition, backers, masterKey>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ doorOpen \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ canister \in Machines \cup {NoMach}
  /\ petition \in Machines \cup {NoMach}
  /\ backers \subseteq Controllers
  /\ masterKey \in BOOLEAN

\* The canister is a single critical resource: the open door belongs to the
\* holder, the holder's door is open, and no vote runs while it is handed out.
CanisterHeldAlone ==
  /\ \A m \in Machines : doorOpen[m] => canister = m
  /\ canister # NoMach => doorOpen[canister]
  /\ petition # NoMach => canister = NoMach

Init ==
  /\ doorOpen = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
  /\ canister = NoMach
  /\ petition = NoMach
  /\ backers = {}
  /\ masterKey = FALSE

Petition(m) ==
  /\ petition = NoMach
  /\ canister = NoMach
  /\ ~masterKey
  /\ petition' = m
  /\ backers' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorOpen, canister, masterKey>>

Back(c) ==
  /\ petition # NoMach
  /\ c \notin backers
  /\ backers' = backers \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorOpen, canister, petition, masterKey>>

\* Nothing short of a quorum opens the door.
Open ==
  /\ petition # NoMach
  /\ Cardinality(backers) >= Quorum
  /\ canister = NoMach
  /\ canister' = petition
  /\ doorOpen' = [doorOpen EXCEPT ![petition] = TRUE]
  /\ petition' = NoMach
  /\ backers' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED masterKey

Close(m) ==
  /\ doorOpen[m]
  /\ doorOpen' = [doorOpen EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
  /\ canister' = NoMach
  /\ UNCHANGED <<petition, backers, masterKey>>

\* The master key outranks the vote.
MasterOpen(m) ==

  /\ canister = NoMach
  /\ masterKey' = TRUE
  /\ canister' = m
  /\ doorOpen' = [doorOpen EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
  /\ petition' = NoMach
  /\ backers' = {}

MasterDrop ==
  /\ masterKey
  /\ canister = NoMach
  /\ masterKey' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorOpen, canister, petition, backers>>

Next ==
  \/ Open
  \/ MasterDrop
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Back(c)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Petition(m) \/ Close(m) \/ MasterOpen(m)

SomeBack == \E c \in Controllers : Back(c)

Spec ==

  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(SomeBack)
  /\ WF_vars(Open)

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {mcX, mcY}
    Controllers = {cr1, cr2, cr3}
    Quorum = 2
    NoMach = noMach
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CanisterHeldAlone
PROPERTY EveryPetitionResolved
nl:
A vending machine network shares one cash canister between all its machines.
The canister is the critical resource: at any moment at most one machine may
have its cash door open onto it, and the machine with its door open must be
exactly the machine the canister has been handed to.

A machine cannot open its own door. It puts a petition to the network's
controllers, and the controllers back it one at a time; the door only opens once
a quorum of controllers has backed the standing petition. The field technician
carries a master key that outranks the vote entirely.

Six things can happen. Petition: with no petition standing, the canister free
and the master key not in use, a machine puts up a petition and the backing list
starts empty. Back: a controller that has not yet backed the standing petition
backs it. Open: once the backing list has reached quorum and the canister is
free, the canister is handed to the petitioning machine, its cash door opens,
and the petition and backing list are cleared. Close: the machine whose door is
open closes it and the canister goes free. MasterOpen: with the master key not
in use and the canister free, the technician engages the master key, hands the
canister straight to a machine whose door opens, and tears up any standing
petition. MasterDrop: with the master key in use and the canister free, the
technician puts the master key away.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any machine with its cash door open is exactly the machine the
canister was handed to, the machine holding the canister always has its door
open, and no petition is ever standing while the canister is handed out -- so
two machines can never be on the canister at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every petition that is put up is eventually resolved and
taken off the table.

---- MODULE W4Od5m6p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Slots, Instances, Players, NoInst, NoPlayer, FullTtl

ASSUME NoInst \notin Instances
ASSUME NoPlayer \notin Players

VARIABLES pool, leaseOf, ttl, occupant, seated

vars == <<pool, leaseOf, ttl, occupant, seated>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \subseteq Slots
  /\ leaseOf \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {NoInst}]
  /\ ttl \in [Slots -> 0 .. FullTtl]
  /\ occupant \in [Slots -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
  /\ seated \subseteq Players

\* Free, leased and filled are three disjoint states for a slot, which is what
\* stops two players being dropped into the same one.
NoSlotDoubleFilled ==
  /\ pool = {s \in Slots : leaseOf[s] = NoInst /\ occupant[s] = NoPlayer}
  /\ \A s \in Slots : leaseOf[s] # NoInst => occupant[s] = NoPlayer /\ ttl[s] > 0
  /\ \A s \in Slots : leaseOf[s] = NoInst => ttl[s] = 0
  /\ seated = {p \in Players : \E s \in Slots : occupant[s] = p}

Init ==
  /\ pool = Slots
  /\ leaseOf = [s \in Slots |-> NoInst]
  /\ ttl = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ occupant = [s \in Slots |-> NoPlayer]
  /\ seated = {}

Lease(i, s) ==
  /\ s \in pool
  /\ pool' = pool \ {s}
  /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![s] = i]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = FullTtl]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, seated>>

Tick(s) ==
  /\ leaseOf[s] # NoInst
  /\ ttl[s] > 1
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = ttl[s] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, leaseOf, occupant, seated>>

\* A lapsed lease puts the slot straight back into the shared pool.
Lapse(s) ==
  /\ leaseOf[s] # NoInst
  /\ ttl[s] = 1
  /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![s] = NoInst]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, seated>>

Seat(i, s, p) ==
  /\ leaseOf[s] = i
  /\ ttl[s] > 0
  /\ p \notin seated
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ seated' = seated \cup {p}
  /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![s] = NoInst]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED pool

Leave(s) ==
  /\ occupant[s] # NoPlayer
  /\ seated' = seated \ {occupant[s]}
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = NoPlayer]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOf, ttl>>

Next ==
  \E s \in Slots :
    \/ Tick(s)
    \/ Lapse(s)
    \/ Leave(s)
    \/ \E i \in Instances :
         \/ Lease(i, s)
         \/ \E p \in Players : Seat(i, s, p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker is run as two independent matchmaker
instances that share one pool of lobby slots. A slot may only ever be filled by
one player, so an instance is not allowed to drop a player into a slot it has
not first taken out of the shared free pool.

To take a slot, an instance puts a lease on it, which removes the slot from the
free pool and starts a countdown. The lease only lasts while the countdown is
running; if the countdown runs out before the instance seats anybody, the lease
lapses and the slot goes straight back into the free pool for either instance to
try again.

Five things can happen. Lease: an instance takes a slot out of the shared free
pool, marks the slot as leased to itself and starts the countdown at full.
Tick: a leased slot whose countdown has more than one tick left drops by one.
Lapse: a leased slot whose countdown is on its last tick loses its lease, zeroes
its countdown and goes back into the free pool. Seat: the instance holding a
live lease on a slot drops an unseated player into it, which ends the lease,
zeroes the countdown and leaves the slot filled rather than back in the pool.
Leave: the player in a filled slot quits, emptying the slot and putting it back
into the free pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared free pool is exactly the set of slots that are
neither leased nor filled, a slot under lease is always empty and always has its
countdown still running, an unleased slot always has a zero countdown, and the
seated players are exactly the players sitting in slots -- so the same slot can
never be allocated to two players.

CONSTANTS

    StartBacklog = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoUnauthorisedRun
PROPERTY EveryBacklogDrains
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash bays, each with its own backlog of
cars waiting on it. A bay operator is not authorised to run the machinery on its
own say-so: a single duty token walks a fixed ring of bays, and only the bay the
token is currently parked at may pick up a run permit. A permit picked up by a
bay other than the token's bay, or a permit still held after the shift
supervisor has locked the line out, would be an unauthorised run.

The token only moves on once the bay it is parked at has no permit outstanding
and no cars left in its backlog. The shift supervisor can lock the whole line
out, but only while no bay is holding a permit, and can unlock it again.

Six things can happen. Grant: with the line not locked out and the token's bay
holding no permit, that bay picks up the run permit. Wash: the bay holding the
permit runs one car out of its own backlog through the machinery. Revoke: the
bay holding the permit hands it back. Pass: with the token's bay holding no
permit and its backlog empty, the token moves one step round the ring. Lockout:
with the line not already locked out and no bay holding a permit, the shift
supervisor locks the line out. Unlock: the shift supervisor unlocks the line.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The only bay that can be holding a run permit is the bay the
token is parked at, and no bay holds a run permit while the line is locked out,
so no unauthorised or superseded bay ever runs the machinery.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bay's backlog is eventually washed down to nothing.

  /\ dispensed \subseteq Scripts
  /\ claim \in [Stations -> Scripts \cup {NoRx}]
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN

\* Handing over stock is irreversible, so a dispensed prescription can never be
\* outstanding again and can never be sitting under a station's claim.

  /\ outstanding \cup dispensed = Scripts
  /\ \A s \in Stations : claim[s] # NoRx => claim[s] \in outstanding
  /\ override => \A s \in Stations : claim[s] = NoRx

  /\ dispensed = {}
  /\ claim = [s \in Stations |-> NoRx]
  /\ override = FALSE

  /\ claim[token] = NoRx
  /\ token' = NextStation(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<outstanding, dispensed, claim, override>>

Claim(r) ==

  /\ claim[token] = NoRx
  /\ r \in outstanding
  /\ \A s \in Stations : claim[s] # r
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![token] = r]

  /\ claim[token] # NoRx
  /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {claim[token]}
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {claim[token]}
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![token] = NoRx]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, override>>

  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![s] = NoRx]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, outstanding, dispensed, override>>

\* The pharmacist-in-charge outranks the ring and voids every claim.
TakeOver ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ override' = TRUE
  /\ claim' = [s \in Stations |-> NoRx]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, outstanding, dispensed>>

OverrideDispense(r) ==
  /\ override
  /\ r \in outstanding
  /\ outstanding' = outstanding \ {r}
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, claim, override>>

StandDown ==
  /\ override
  /\ override' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, outstanding, dispensed, claim>>

Next ==
  \/ Pass
  \/ Dispense
  \/ TakeOver
  \/ StandDown
  \/ \E r \in Scripts : Claim(r) \/ OverrideDispense(r)
  \/ \E s \in Stations : Release(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    NumStations = 2
    Scripts = {rxA, rxB}
    NoRx = noRx
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DispensedOnlyOnce
nl:
A pharmacy dispenses controlled prescriptions from a bank of dispensing
stations. Handing a controlled prescription over the counter is irreversible:
the stock has left the safe and the register has been signed, so a prescription
must never be dispensed a second time.

The right to dispense is carried by a single duty token that walks a fixed ring
of stations. Only the station the token is parked at may claim a prescription
off the outstanding list, and a prescription already claimed by some station
cannot be claimed by another. The pharmacist-in-charge holds an override that
outranks the token entirely; engaging it tears up every station's claim.

Seven things can happen. Pass: with the token's station holding no claim, the
token moves one step round the ring. Claim: with no override in force, the
token's station takes an outstanding prescription that no station has claimed.
Dispense: the token's station hands over the prescription it has claimed, which
moves the prescription off the outstanding list into the dispensed register and
clears the claim. Release: a station gives up its claim without dispensing.
TakeOver: the pharmacist-in-charge engages the override, which tears up every
station's claim. OverrideDispense: with the override in force, the pharmacist
hands over an outstanding prescription directly. StandDown: the
pharmacist-in-charge disengages the override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every prescription is either outstanding or dispensed and never
both, every claim held by a station names a prescription that is still
outstanding, and no station holds a claim while the pharmacist's override is in
force -- so no prescription can be dispensed twice.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Brokers, NumLevels, Depth, NoBroker

ASSUME NoBroker \notin Brokers

Levels == 1 .. NumLevels
Opening == NumLevels * Depth

VARIABLES bookClaim, levelClaim, onBook, allocated, returned

vars == <<bookClaim, levelClaim, onBook, allocated, returned>>

RECURSIVE Resting(_)
Resting(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN onBook[l] + Resting(S \ {l})

TypeOK ==
  /\ bookClaim \in Brokers \cup {NoBroker}
  /\ levelClaim \in [Levels -> Brokers \cup {NoBroker}]
  /\ onBook \in [Levels -> 0 .. Depth]
  /\ allocated \in 0 .. Opening
  /\ returned \in 0 .. Opening

\* Shares are conserved across the cross, and the two-level discipline holds:
\* a fine claim always belongs to whoever holds the coarse claim.
SharesConserved ==
  /\ Resting(Levels) + allocated + returned = Opening
  /\ \A l \in Levels : levelClaim[l] # NoBroker => bookClaim = levelClaim[l]

Init ==
  /\ bookClaim = NoBroker
  /\ levelClaim = [l \in Levels |-> NoBroker]
  /\ onBook = [l \in Levels |-> Depth]
  /\ allocated = 0
  /\ returned = 0

TakeBook(b) ==
  /\ bookClaim = NoBroker
  /\ bookClaim' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<levelClaim, onBook, allocated, returned>>

\* Coarse first, then fine, and only on a level that still has interest.
TakeLevel(b, l) ==
  /\ bookClaim = b
  /\ levelClaim[l] = NoBroker
  /\ onBook[l] > 0
  /\ levelClaim' = [levelClaim EXCEPT ![l] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookClaim, onBook, allocated, returned>>

Cross(b, l) ==
  /\ levelClaim[l] = b
  /\ onBook[l] > 0
  /\ onBook' = [onBook EXCEPT ![l] = onBook[l] - 1]
  /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookClaim, levelClaim, returned>>

Pull(b, l) ==
  /\ levelClaim[l] = b
  /\ onBook[l] > 0
  /\ onBook' = [onBook EXCEPT ![l] = onBook[l] - 1]
  /\ returned' = returned + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookClaim, levelClaim, allocated>>

StandDown(b) ==
  /\ bookClaim = b
  /\ bookClaim' = NoBroker
  /\ levelClaim' = [l \in Levels |->
       IF levelClaim[l] = b THEN NoBroker ELSE levelClaim[l]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onBook, allocated, returned>>

Next ==
  \E b \in Brokers :
    \/ TakeBook(b)
    \/ StandDown(b)
    \/ \E l \in Levels : TakeLevel(b, l) \/ Cross(b, l) \/ Pull(b, l)

SomeTakeBook == \E b \in Brokers : TakeBook(b)
SomeTakeLevel == \E b \in Brokers, l \in Levels : TakeLevel(b, l)
SomeFill == \E b \in Brokers, l \in Levels : Cross(b, l) \/ Pull(b, l)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(SomeTakeBook)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeTakeLevel)
  /\ SF_vars(SomeFill)

BookEventuallyClears ==
  (allocated + returned < Opening) ~> (allocated + returned = Opening)

CONSTANTS
    Brokers = {brA, brB}
    NumLevels = 2
    Depth = 2
    NoBroker = noBroker
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SharesConserved
PROPERTY BookEventuallyClears
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction. The sell interest sitting on the book
is split across price levels, and every share on the book has to end up in
exactly one of two places by the time the auction crosses: allocated to a buyer,
or returned to the seller unfilled. Shares are never created and never
destroyed.

Brokers work the book under a two-level discipline. A broker first takes the
coarse claim on the whole book, and only then may it take the fine claim on an
individual price level, and only a level that still has interest on it. Giving
up the coarse claim also gives up every fine claim the same broker was holding.
No broker ever drops out of the auction, but a broker can be slow: it may sit on
the coarse claim for a long time without doing anything with it.

Five things can happen. TakeBook: a broker takes the coarse claim on the book
while it is free. TakeLevel: the broker holding the coarse claim takes the free
fine claim on a price level that still has interest on it. Cross: the broker
holding the fine claim on a level with interest crosses one share off that
level and allocates it to a buyer. Pull: the broker holding the fine claim on a
level with interest takes one share off that level and returns it unfilled to
the seller. StandDown: the broker holding the coarse claim gives it up along
with every fine claim it holds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shares still on the book, the shares allocated to buyers
and the shares returned unfilled always add up to the auction's opening size,
and any fine claim on a price level is held by the very broker that holds the
coarse claim on the book.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every share still sitting on the book is eventually either
allocated to a buyer or returned unfilled.
